brief: A closed electronics enclosure with a louvred vent so the board inside can breathe.

requirements.requirement: Closed enclosure for an electronics board
requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full with cover:0,0,0;full;top and solid caps on all six faces (cap:0,0,0;*;30/90/150/210/270/330); joints locked.

requirements.requirement: Louvred vent so the board can breathe
requirements.evidence: port:0#0,0#0 is a hex-port-louvre in port slot 0 of the base. The catalogue says it vents a closed cell. The configurator accepted it alongside all six caps and the mesh check came back clear. I couldn't see it in the view, though, so I haven't confirmed visually that the vent opens to the outside. How much cooling it gives depends on the board, and the configurator doesn't check that.

finish.summary: A one-cell closed enclosure: a full hex base with a solid top cover and solid end caps on all six side faces. A louvre port (hex-port-louvre) sits in port slot 0 of the base as the vent. capOpenFaces and lockJoints were run. check_build shows no rule issues and meshClash "clear". 12 printed parts in the BOM, about 485 g and 696 min. I added no props because the catalogue has no circuit-board prop, and anything inside would be hidden by the lid. I didn't get a usable view of the vent: the look call at the port returned nothing.
